summary: Heerenveen charges for parking in the centre Monday to Saturday (9:00-20:00, Thursday to 21:00, free on Sundays and national holidays); for 2026 the council set 1.90 euros per hour (9.00 euro day rate above 4 hours 45 minutes) on the street in the centre, 2.50 / 5.00 euros per half / whole day on the west side of the station, and the municipal Geerts Willigenplein garage charges 1.90 euros per hour with a 7.00 euro daily maximum. Annual permit fees are 105 euros for the standard permit categories, and a January 2026 Mobility Fund ordinance lets developers buy out parking obligations in the centre. The policy direction in the October 2025 mobility programme is to move parking from street to garages and to green the squares, centred on an underground two-level garage of about 350 spaces under Burgemeester Kuperusplein (14.7 million euros in 2022, a January 2024 proposal to raise it to 24.1 million euros, and still described as to be built in October 2025); a March 2022 survey found 73 percent Saturday-afternoon occupancy in the eastern centre and a 2024 council paper cites more than 90 percent on Saturday afternoons. Around Sportstad, the Abe Lenstra stadium and Thialf the council plans to improve over 2,000 spaces, make lot P6 free and extend paid parking towards the A32, and to consider a transferium at the stations; public charging stood at about 80 locations and 200 charge points in 2025. The national register lists the 144-space P+R Stationsplein as run by NS, but no official occupancy statement or current NS tariff for it was found.

items.text: The municipal council adopted the 2026 parking tax ordinance on 11 December 2025, in force from 1 January 2026. On-street parking at machines in the centre costs 1.90 euros per hour (billed in 10-cent units) with a day rate of 9.00 euros for stays longer than 4 hours 45 minutes; at the west side of the railway station it costs 2.50 euros for a half day and 5.00 euros for a whole day.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelasting 2026 (Heerenveen)

items.text: The 2026 ordinance sets annual parking permit fees of 105 euros for the standard permit categories (articles 3(3)(a)-(b) of the Parkeerverordening 2021) and 378 euros for another category (articles 3(3)(c) and (e)), 51 euros for social institutions, and a supplementary assessment fee of 83.90 euros. Holders of a disabled parking card are exempt at machines and no remission (kwijtschelding) is granted.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelasting 2026 (Heerenveen)

items.text: For comparison, the 2025 ordinance (council of 19 December 2024) set the centre rate at 1.80 euros per hour with a 9.00 euro day rate above 5 hours, the same station-west rates of 2.50 and 5.00 euros, and a standard permit fee of 102 euros. The 2026 rates are therefore an increase of about 6 percent per hour in the centre, with the station rates unchanged.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelasting 2025 (Heerenveen, expired 31-12-2025)

items.text: The municipality itself sets the tariffs for its Geerts Willigenplein garage in the centre (college decision of 18 November 2025, in force 1 January 2026): short stay 1.90 euros per hour (1.80 in 2025) with a 7.00 euro daily maximum, and subscriptions of 40 euros per month (Mon-Fri) or 60 euros per month (7/7). Paid hours are 9:00-20:00 (Thursday to 21:00, Sunday and national holidays free) and short-stay entry is open 5:00-22:00.

The college's Aanwijzingsbesluit parkeren 2023 (14 March 2023, in force 15 March 2023) designates paid and permit parking in the centre and in surrounding 'schil' streets. Payment applies Mon-Fri 9:00-20:00, Thursday evening shopping until 21:00 and Saturday 9:00-20:00, with free parking on Sundays and national holidays; machines take coins, bank cards or phone payment.

The same 2023 decision lists permit-only parking areas around the centre (zones VN1, VN2, NH1, NH2, SG1, SG2); permit-only hours are Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00, and Mon-Sat 9:00-17:00 in the station-side zones SG1 and SG2. The Beugel zone excludes the park-and-ride lot on the west side of the NS station, and a paid lot between the station and Beugel is listed under the 'station' area. The legislation database shows this decision as valid from 15 March 2023 'to date' when read on 21 October 2026.

On 29 January 2026 the council adopted a Mobility Fund (Mobiliteitsfonds) ordinance for the town centre: developers who cannot provide the parking required by the municipal parking norms can pay a buy-out per space, set at 6,318 / 12,636 / 18,954 euros for low / middle / high-segment housing and 12,636 euros for other uses (January 2026 prices). The municipality must build the bought-out spaces within ten years or refund the money; the area is bounded by a 500 metre walk to the Burgemeester Kuperusplein and Geerts Willigen car parks.

A traffic decision of 22 September 2025 bans parking on the northern part of Burgemeester Kuperusplein (Friday 22:00 to Saturday 19:00) so that the Saturday market can move there while the Sieversstraat, Gemeenteplein and Wettertoer area is redeveloped from late October 2025. The decision calls the plein an important visitor car park and states that on the busiest moments there is ample space in the Geerts Willigen garage and at Veldschans and Abe Lenstraboulevard.
items.source_title: Verkeersbesluit parkeerverbod noordelijk deel Burgemeester Kuperusplein (Gemeenteblad 2025, 418408)

items.text: The national parking open-data register (NPR, static record read on 21 October 2026) lists P+R Stationsplein (Stationsplein 12) as a 144-space park-and-ride operated by Nederlandse Spoorwegen, with no charging points and tariff entries of 1.14 euros per hour and 9.02 euros per day. These register tariffs differ from the municipal west-station rates of 2.50 / 5.00 euros in the 2026 ordinance, so the register entry may be out of date.
items.source_title: RDW NPR static data: P+R Stationsplein (Heerenveen)

items.text: A March 2022 parking pressure survey for the eastern centre found Saturday afternoon to be the busiest moment, with 407 of 560 visitor and permit spaces occupied (73 percent); in the adjoining Schilwijk Oost 21 of 69 spaces were used (30 percent). The study treats 90 percent occupancy as the practical limit before search traffic builds up.
items.source_title: Dynamische parkeerbalans Centrum-Oost Heerenveen (annex to zoning plan Burgemeester Kuperusplein e.o.)

items.text: A council proposal for extra funding of the Burgemeester Kuperusplein garage states that recent counts show Saturday-afternoon occupancy of the centre's parking already above 90 percent, causing extra search traffic, and that the planned greening of three squares (30-60 percent of surface spaces lost) must be offset underground. The text says housing growth of at least 2,000 homes to 2030 will raise parking pressure further.
items.source_title: Raadsvoorstel Aanvullend krediet parkeergarage BK Plein (Z.22.380040, January 2024)

items.text: A council proposal (reference Z.22.380040) proposed an underground two-level garage with about 350 spaces under Burgemeester Kuperusplein instead of a one-level 250-space option, for an investment credit of 14.7 million euros. It also proposed extra parking at Verlengde Veldschans (a plan-map idea of about 150 spaces) and Molenplein Zuid, and listed charging points, number-plate recognition and bicycle parking as design basics; the January 2024 paper below says the council backed this in December 2022. In January 2024 the college proposed an extra 9.4 million euros, raising the total to 24.1 million euros, and reported about a year of delay; I did not find the final decision or a construction schedule.
items.source_title: Raadsvoorstel Parkeren & inrichting openbare ruimte centrumontwikkelingen Heerenveen (Z.22.380040) and Raadsvoorstel Aanvullend krediet parkeergarage BK Plein (January 2024)

items.text: On 13 May 2025 the council adopted the Gebiedsvisie A32 (published 10 February 2026) for the area around Sportstad. It plans to extend paid parking up to the A32 and make the east-side lot P6 free, to improve over 2,000 spaces (P2, P6, P8 redesigned) and to replace the vanishing lots P3 and P9 with a larger lot south of P9; P6 and P8 are said to be underused because of poor access, with P6 used mainly at stadium events. Paid parking in Sportstad is listed only as a tertiary priority, so these are plans. The October 2025 mobility programme adds that demand rises sharply during top-sport matches and floats a transferium or mobility hub at Abe Lenstra station and/or the IJsstadion event station near Thialf.
items.source_title: Gebiedsvisie A32 Heerenveen (Gemeenteblad 2026, 61839) and Omgevingsprogramma Mobiliteit (Gemeenteblad 2025, 469488)

items.text: The same mobility programme says visitors to the centre are to be steered to two central garages, Geerts Willigen and the still-to-be-built Burgemeester Kuperusplein garage (350 underground spaces), by making on-street parking more expensive than the garages. The aim is a gradual shift of spaces from street to garage to free space for greenery, with no net loss of capacity; new central developments must park on their own site, use central facilities or pay into the Mobility Fund.
items.source_title: Omgevingsprogramma Mobiliteit 'We geven elkaar de ruimte' (Gemeenteblad 2025, 469488)

items.text: The mobility programme reports that electric vehicles in the municipality nearly tripled in three years and that public charging has grown to 80 public locations with 200 charge points. It cites grid congestion and delays in placing charge posts as bottlenecks and aims for sufficient charging near shopping centres, car parks, residential areas and transport hubs.
items.source_title: Omgevingsprogramma Mobiliteit 'We geven elkaar de ruimte' (Gemeenteblad 2025, 469488)

items.text: In answers to council questions (received 7 August 2024) the municipality reported about 75 public AC charging locations on municipal land (28 TotalEnergies, 18 Allego, 28 Park'n'Charge), seven more expected soon and 17 requests pending. The TotalEnergies concession places posts for requests up to 1 December 2025 and operates them until 1 December 2032; its price was 0.35 euros per kWh incl. VAT in August 2024 (Allego 0.82 euros per kWh).
items.source_title: Technische vragen: Tarieven openbare laadpalen in de gemeente Heerenveen (Heerenveen Lokaal, 2024)

items.text: The club's visitor page (read on 21 October 2026) advises match-day drivers to use the stadium lots P3, P5A and P6, which need a single-match or season parking card, or the free carpool site Plein Noord (about 20 minutes' walk), or paid parking in the centre. It says supporters who park in residential streets will be strictly checked by police and the municipality, and that the station is about a 20 minute walk from the stadium.

A programme newsletter issued ahead of a 9 January 2025 information meeting reported that the Molenplein Zuid parking works were finished and that the Verlengde Veldschans would be made permanent with about 150 spaces in two phases, with works expected from mid-February 2025 and the lot closed for 3-4 months. It also announced two extra charge posts (four connections) at the existing charging facility there.

gaps: Municipal website www.heerenveen.nl was showing 'Website offline' (security notice) when read on 21 October 2026, so the municipal parking, permit and project pages could not be read; heerenveen.nl/parkeren and /centrum returned 404.

www.programmacentrumheerenveen.nl returned 503 'Suspended Site'; no current construction schedule, contractor or opening date for the Burgemeester Kuperusplein garage was found (latest dated source on its status: Gemeenteblad 30 October 2025 calls it 'nog te bouwen').

Final council decision on the January 2024 supplementary credit (9.4 million euros) and the annex 'memo parkeerbalans' to the November 2022 proposal were not opened; the raadsinformatie site (heerenveen.bestuurlijkeinformatie.nl) has no usable search without JavaScript.
No official source found on Thialf or Abe Lenstra stadium event-parking arrangements beyond the club page and the council programmes; thialf.nl pages tried returned 404.

No measured or official occupancy figures for the station park-and-ride (P+R Stationsplein, run by NS per the NPR register) or the Geerts Willigenplein garage; the only utilisation statements found are the March 2022 survey and the January 2024 'more than 90 percent on Saturday afternoon' statement for the centre.
NS pages for the station P+R (current tariff, capacity) were not opened; the NPR register tariff (1.14 euros per hour) conflicts with the municipal station-west rates (2.50 / 5.00 euros), unresolved.
Number of spaces in the Geerts Willigenplein garage and in centre surface lots was not found in a current source; the Parkeervisie 2017 and Nota Parkeernormen were not opened.
Low-emission/environmental zone or pedestrian-zone rules for the centre were not found in any source read.
